svg.text: One tree model. Server truth. Offline working state.
Persistent Merkle trees • Immutable nodes • Durable operation replay • Named checkpoints
One head per owner + collection; old states survive through retained roots.
Owner-partitioned cache and edits; works without a network connection.
rootHash identifies the complete current state.
Pin an existing root; no snapshot-building draft.
Leaf: record IDs → complete record values.
Immutable; branches reference this same table.
Different payload with same opId → reject.
Stored atomically with nodes and head update.
References stay within the same owner.
All four tables belong to an authenticated owner.
Receipts are scoped to the same owner + collection as the head.
No live todo rows: records live in leaves. No per-record sync revisions.
Bounded checkpoint list; each listed tree is cached.
opId remains stable across all retries.
Same node format and hashes as the server.
Caches confirmed and pinned checkpoint trees.
Working nodes may remain in memory.
Rebuild on startup; update in memory.
Expose rows to the UI through TanStack DB.
Publish only after its full tree is cached.
Each pointer: 0..1 node; each node: 0..* refs
All references use the same ownerId.
Three durable stores; no persisted workingRoot or separate checkpoint store.
Persist each edit in the outbox before considering it safely saved.
Confirm atomically: advance the cached baseline and remove acknowledged edits.
Send operations + opIds. Server applies them to its latest root, never blindly installs a client root.
Subscribe to head changes; fetch missing nodes by hash. Publish the new local state only when its required nodes are ready.
Dashed lines = logical references, not SQL foreign keys. Root null = empty collection. All hash lookups are owner-scoped.
Node hashes cover a canonical, versioned payload. One node may have many parents; no parent pointer is stored.
Garbage collection must retain server heads/checkpoints and client confirmed/offline-pinned roots. Merkle trees do not merge conflicts by themselves.
PROPOSAL Based on OS2’s existing outbox, receipts, and immutable checkpoint trees. Names and fields above describe the proposed replacement architecture.
